description: We are a team of young explorers from Classes IV and V at Benchmark Junior School, G.T. Road Campus, Islamabad. For the 2026 challenge, "The Next Frontier", we are building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. It's a fun, kid-friendly way for children to learn what astronauts do and train like one. They practise mission skills, learn about life in space and follow the journey from Earth to the Moon and beyond.
summary:
Outpost Mars is a turn-based browser game for ages 7 to 12. The player is the Mission Planner of a small Mars outpost. Every sol (Mars day) they share a few solar power tokens between keeping the crew alive, exploring, building and science, while real solar storms recorded by NASA test the plan.

It teaches three true things: power is limited, radiation dose adds up, and Earth can't help instantly. A storm warning from Earth arrives the next morning, so the player must call one sol early.

The campaign has three chapters and 28 sols. Chapter 3 plays the real Sun of 8 to 17 May 2024, with measured solar particle storms from NASA DONKI on 10, 11 and 13 May. Free play uses the last 10 or 20 real days, live.

It runs from one public link on a phone or laptop, with no login, no cookies and no personal data. Every number in the game shows its NASA source or is labelled a game simplification.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Outpost Mars is a Mars mission game for children aged 7 to 12. It opens with a one-minute movie of the trip from Earth to Mars, then a learn-by-doing tutorial. Each sol has five parts: Sunrise, Day, Sunset, Night and Report. The player only chooses during the Day, and the game waits for them, so good choices matter and fast clicking does not.

Five meters keep the crew alive or count radiation: Air, Food, Water, Warmth and Dose. Each shows a bar, a number, a state word and a preview of what tonight will do, so a child sees the result of a choice before making it. Solar panels give 6, 4 or 2 power tokens depending on the weather. Trips to four sites bring back materials, the base grows through seven fixed slots, and there is not enough metal to build everything, so every player must choose.

THE THREE LESSONS

1. Power is limited. You cannot do or build everything.

2. Radiation dose adds up. Dose is one budget for all 28 sols and never goes down.

3. Earth can't help instantly. A storm warning arrives the next morning.

HOW IT USES NASA DATA

Storm days come from NASA DONKI: solar energetic particle events measured by instruments. Chapter 3 plays 8 to 17 May 2024, with storms on 10, 11 and 13 May. Chapters 1 and 2 use 1 to 18 July 2019, a quiet window with no recorded event. Free play "Real Sun Now" asks DONKI for the last 10 or 20 days and is labelled LIVE; if NASA cannot be reached it uses an archive labelled with its real dates. Power levels follow the Opportunity rover's power in the June 2018 dust storm. Fact cards use findings from Curiosity, Perseverance and MOXIE, and Phoenix. A Data & Credits screen lists every number with its source or a "game simplification" note.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

A child learns why planning ahead matters in space, with real dates and real measurements. Losing explains what happened and why, keeps the science stars and lets the player retry one chapter. Judges can use the "Judges' shortcut" in the Chapter menu to start at Chapter 3.

HOW IT WAS MADE

Tools: TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, three.js for the 3D scenes, Vitest for tests, and Vercel for hosting with one small server function for the live NASA data. The rules are a separate engine with 110 automated tests. Robot players ran 2,000 campaigns each to check the balance: careful planners win 97 to 100%, a casual player about 37%, a player who never calls Earth about 4%, and a reckless explorer 0%.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Young players: one new idea per chapter, a word and an icon on every button, read-aloud, and no time pressure. Privacy: no accounts, cookies, tracking or names. Honesty: live and archived data are always labelled, and simplifications are named.

USE OF AI

The students designed the rules, numbers, chapters and lessons. The team's adult mentor used Claude (Anthropic) to write the program code and tests. In this version the on-screen words and the 3D pictures were also made with Claude as placeholders. This is stated in the game's Data & Credits screen and in the demo.
dataRefs: NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information), CCMC
DONKI Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) web service: storms of 8–17 May 2024
NASA Opportunity rover (power in the June 2018 dust storm)
NASA Perseverance rover and MOXIE (oxygen made on Mars; seven-month trip)
NASA Phoenix lander (water ice under the soil)
NASA International Space Station (water recovery; plants grown in space)
